# The bound of a sum of two limbs, as a function of the number of additions

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bound_sum_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Numbers of `T` that bound expressions of $m$ from above, valid when the mask $\mathit{ok}$ is true:

$$g \ge \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2})}{1 - m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2})}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $m = 0$ or $m \ge 1$, as a number of terms is.
- The format contains $\tfrac12$: $\eta \le \tfrac12$, as `float` and `double` do.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2}) \le \frac{1}{2}$.
- when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $g \ge \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2})}{1 - m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2})}$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bound_sum_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BoundKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BoundKernels.v), against `bound_sum_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bound_sum_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bound_sum_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m : R,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  (m = 0 \/ 1 <= m) ->
  eta emin <= / 2 ->
  let '(g, ok) := bound_sum_2 emin prec tie_even m in
  fmt emin prec g /\
  (ok = true -> (m * ((3 / (1 - (4 * u prec))) * u prec ^ 2)) <= (1 / 2)) /\
  (ok = true -> ((m * ((3 / (1 - (4 * u prec))) * u prec ^ 2)) / (1 - (m * ((3 / (1 - (4 * u prec))) * u prec ^ 2)))) <= g).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bound_sum_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the exported bound of a sum as a function of n (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bound_sum_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bound_sum_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The exported bound of a sum of 2-limb numbers, as a function of the number m of additions on a
# path of the summation tree (milestone2.md, "The bound as a function of n"). When the mask ok is
# true, m eps <= 1/2 and g >= gamma_m(eps) = m eps / (1 - m eps), with eps the proved unit of
# add_2_2, for m = 0 or m >= 1, in a format that contains 1/2. ok is true at least when
# m eps <= 1/5; when it is false the header returns +inf, which claims nothing. Only products and
# sums of nonnegative numbers, so that the same listing runs in constant evaluation with plain
# products (the rule of the product).
#   a  >= m eps                         (the constant holds a factor 1 + u and eta / 2)
#   aa >= (1 + u) (m eps + eta / 2)
#   w  >= 1 + 2 a                       (for a <= 1/2)
#   g  >= m eps (1 + 2 m eps) >= gamma_m(eps)   (for m eps <= 1/2)

a  = prod(m, const up((1+u)*(unit(add_2_2)+eta/2)))
aa = prod(m, const up((1+u)^2*(unit(add_2_2)+eta)))
# d = 2a. milestone2.md writes add(a, a), which GCC turns into a * 2 and contracts into the
# next addition (rule R1 refuses it); the opaque product has the same value.
d  = prod(a, const up(2))
w  = add(d, const up(1+2*u))
g  = prod(aa, w)
ok = le(a, const up(1/4))
```
